newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Elf Nigeria to spend $500 mln on gas.
newsitem.headline: Elf Nigeria to spend $500 mln on gas.

text.p: Elf Petroleum Nigeria Limited is to spend $500 million to develop a gas field that will feed Nigeria's liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant, a company spokesman said on Monday.
"We will soon lay the foundation of the Ubite gas project from where our contribution of gas supply to the LNG will come," he said.

Elf, a joint venture between state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) and Elf-Aquitaine of France, has 15 percent equity in the $4 billion Nigerian LNG due to come on stream in 1999 in the southeastern Bonny oil-producing area.

A director of the joint venture company, Jean Daniel Blasco, wrote in the current edition of the "Nigerian Elf" quarterly magazine that the Elf group's financial involvement in the LNG project was $600 million.
The spokesman said the spending on Ubite gas field was seperate from Elf's equity participation in the LNG project.
"Nigeria for Elf is strategic given the financial involvement of the group," Blasco wrote.
He said Elf's crude oil production in Nigeria was currently around 140,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 90,000 bpd in 1993.
"There are new prospects deep offshore. There is possibility of new acreages," Blasco said.
